cues.en: Some of the most often repeated programming advice, especially to beginner programmers,
cues.zh: 最常重复的编程建议之一，尤其是给初学者们的，

cues.en: is that they should be writing clean code.
cues.zh: 就是他们应该编写整洁的代码。

cues.en: And that name is accompanied by a long list of rules that tell you what you should do in order for your code to be clean.
cues.zh: 随之而来的还有一长串规则，告诉你为了让代码变整洁应该做什么。

cues.en: Now, there is no benchmark for this. You cannot actually run something and have it tell you how clean your code is, but there are fairly descriptive rules that tell you what you should be doing. Now, a large portion of these rules don't actually affect the runtime of the code that you write, especially not if it's compiled.
cues.zh: 现在，这并没有一个基准。你实际上无法运行某个东西来让它告诉你代码有多整洁，但确实有一些相当具描述性的规则来告诉你应该做什么。而且，这些规则很大一部分其实并不会影响你编写的代码的运行时，特别是如果它是经过编译的话。

cues.en: And so, there is really no way to objectively assess whether these clean code ideas are good or bad. And we don't necessarily have to because they're fairly arbitrary at that point.
cues.zh: 因此，确实没有办法客观地评估这些整洁代码的理念是好是坏。而且我们也不一定非得去评估，因为在那种情况下它们相当于是随意的。

cues.en: However,
cues.zh: 然而，

cues.en: there are several aspects of clean code. In fact, some of the most important ones that are stated are things we could objectively measure because they do affect the run time of the program that you are writing.
cues.zh: 整洁代码有几个方面。事实上，其中一些最重要、被反复提及的方面其实是我们可以客观衡量的，因为它们确实会影响你编写的程序的运行时。

cues.en: Those are if you go look at a list and pull out the ones that would actually carry through to the code as it is compiled
cues.zh: 如果你去查看一份清单，挑出那些真正能延续到代码编译阶段、

cues.en: and run on the end user's machine. There are things like polymorphism
cues.zh: 并在最终用户的机器上运行的规则。就会发现诸如多态

cues.en: is good, so that's like a plus.
cues.zh: 是好的，所以这算是个加分项。

cues.en: Ifs and switches are bad.
cues.zh: if 和 switch 是不好的。

cues.en: So those are two things you can easily act on. Always use polymorphism if you can. Get rid of if and switch statements.
cues.zh: 所以这是你可以轻松付诸行动的两点。能用多态就尽量用。去掉 if 和 switch 语句。

cues.en: Number two is no internals
cues.zh: 第二点是不要关心内部实现

cues.en: for things.
cues.zh: 针对各种对象。

cues.en: You should never know the internals of something you're working on. So for example, if you write a function that does something, it should always call like a polymorphic function in an object or something like that and it should never like look into the object to see what's actually in there or what kind of object it is. It should never know what like the internals of that thing are ever.
cues.zh: 你永远不应该去了解你所操作的事物的内部实现。比如，如果你写了一个执行某些操作的函数，它应当始终调用对象中的多态函数之类的东西，而绝不应该去查看对象内部来确认里面到底有什么或者这是什么类型的对象。它绝对不应该知道那个事物的内部实现是什么。

cues.en: Number three is functions should be small.
cues.zh: 第三点是函数应该很小。

cues.en: Number four,
cues.zh: 第四点，

cues.en: functions should do one thing.
cues.zh: 函数应该只做一件事。

cues.en: Now, one thing is never really defined in any particular way and I don't really think that's all that actionable, but it is kind of a general rule of thumb you could see affecting how you structure your code. It's sort of taken together with this that you're trying to reduce a function maybe down to the smallest possible thing it could be, let's say.
cues.zh: 现在，“一件事”其实从来没有一个确切的定义，我也觉得这并不是那么具有可操作性，但它算是一个通用的经验法则，你可以看到它如何影响你组织代码的方式。结合这一点来看，你大概是想把一个函数精简到它可能做到的最小事情，暂且这么说吧。

cues.en: Finally, number five is don't repeat yourself or d r y.
cues.zh: 最后，第五点是不要重复自己，即 DRY 原则。

cues.en: In general, if you take all of these things, they are actually fairly specific about how any particular piece of code should be created in order for it to be quote unquote clean.
cues.zh: 总的来说，如果你采纳所有这些原则，它们对于任何特定代码片段该如何编写其实都有相当具体的规定，以此来达到所谓的“整洁”。

cues.en: And so what I would like to ask is, well, if we create a piece of code that follows these rules and is clean,
cues.zh: 所以我想问的是，如果我们编写了一段遵循这些规则且很整洁的代码，

cues.en: how does it perform?
cues.zh: 它的性能表现如何呢？

cues.en: In order to construct what I would consider the most favorable case for a clean code implementation
cues.zh: 为了构建我所认为的对整洁代码实现最有利的场景

cues.en: of something,
cues.zh: 来实现某个功能，

cues.en: I used their own example code because I figured that way I'm not making something up. I'm just using what they actually give as an example of how you should do something.
cues.zh: 我直接用了他们自己的示例代码，因为我想这样我就不是凭空捏造了。我只是在用他们实际给出的示例，来展示你应该如何实现某个功能。

cues.zh: 所以，如果你看整洁代码的示例，会发现这个例子经常被重复。它是一个形状的基类，然后有几个从该基类派生的形状：圆形、三角形、矩形、正方形，如果需要还可以再加一些。

cues.zh: 但我们有一个虚函数，做的类似计算面积的事情，这里的思路是我们更倾向于

cues.zh: 多态

You can see that we just have this little tiny area function and depending on which of the derived classes we have, we will do a different area computation for the square, the rectangle, the triangle, or the circle.
cues.zh: 以及让函数只做一件事、保持简短之类的良好做法。你可以看到我们只有这个小小的面积函数，根据我们持有的是哪个派生类，我们会为正方形、矩形、三角形或圆形做不同的面积计算。

cues.zh: 现在如果我们想象使用这个，

cues.en: if we wanted to find the area of a series of shapes that we pass in, we would expect to see something like this. Now you'll notice I haven't used an iterator here because there was nothing in clean code that suggested you had to use iterators so I figured I would give them the benefit of the doubt and assume they were just going to use a basic for loop that wouldn't have anything that would confuse the compiler.
cues.zh: 如果我们想求传入的一系列形状的面积，我们会期望看到类似这样的代码。你会注意到我这里没有用迭代器，因为整洁代码里没有任何地方暗示你必须用迭代器，所以我想给他们一点信任，假设他们只是要用一个基本的 for 循环，不会有任何让编译器困惑的东西。

cues.en: So here we are, we create an accumulator, we loop over all of the shapes in the array that we're given, we call the area function on them and we return. Now you'll notice these have to be arrays of pointers because we have no idea how big each of these shapes are so unless we were going to parse out the lengths of the shape and use some kind of a skip procedure to go through them, we have to just look at pointers to find out where the shapes actually are.
cues.zh: 于是就是这样，我们创建一个累加器，遍历给定数组中所有的形状，对它们调用面积函数，然后返回。你会注意到这些必须是指针数组，因为我们完全不知道每个形状有多大，所以除非我们要解析形状的长度并用某种跳过过程来遍历它们，否则我们只能看指针来找出形状实际在哪里。

cues.en: Furthermore, you'll see there's a loop carry dependency here. This accumulator is gonna get added to each time so just to make sure that we're not seeing some artifact of the loop, I also included in hand unrolled four times version
cues.zh: 此外，你会看到这里有一个循环携带依赖。这个累加器每次都会被加上去，所以为了确保我们没有看到循环的某种假象，我还加入了一个手动展开四次的版本

cues.en: just to make sure that the CPU has enough to look at to do adds. We break the dependency chain here by having four separate accumulators, otherwise it's the same code. If I run
cues.zh: 只是为了确保CPU有足够的操作来做加法。我们通过使用四个独立的累加器打破了这里的依赖链，否则代码是一样的。如果我运行

cues.en: that code right there,
cues.zh: 那段代码，

cues.en: what I will get is the total number of cycles per shape that are required to do that operation. So I just feed it a big array of shapes and say, how fast can you do these per shape? So we just... How long would it take to do one shape? I time it in two different ways. One is I time with a repeat count of one,
cues.zh: 我会得到每个形状执行该操作所需的总周期数。所以我只是喂给它一个大数组的形状，然后说，每个形状你能多快完成？所以我们只是……完成一个形状需要多长时间？我用两种不同的方式计时。一种是用重复计数为一来计时，

cues.en: and that shows us what happens if you were in a fairly cold cache scenario. So, like, imagine something was like in the l three might be a good example of what that time's gonna be representative of. And then I also do a repeat count version where we try to prime the cache a little bit more. So this is like if it was going to maybe fit into an l two or something or if it was gonna maybe
cues.zh: 这显示了如果你处于一个相当冷的缓存场景会发生什么。所以，想象一下，比如某个东西在L3缓存中，可能是一个很好的例子，说明那个时间会代表什么。然后我还做了一个重复计数的版本，我们试图稍微预热缓存。所以这就像是如果它可能要放入L2缓存之类的，或者如果它可能要

cues.en: have a branch predictor warm up and do something,
cues.zh: 让分支预测器预热并做些什么，

cues.zh: 我们会在这里看到改进。从结果中我们可以看到这里没有太大区别。做这件事大约需要35个周期。如果你真的很幸运，有时可能会降到34左右。所以我们代码的干净版本大约花了35

cues.en: cycles

cues.en: to actually do each shape. That's what we're doing if we use polymorphism,

cues.en: no internals, small, one thing, don't repeat yourself. We're not violating any rules here.

cues.zh: 而是改用 if 或 switch 语句。对吧？我们不再使用虚函数了。我们例程的性能会怎样

cues.en: if we change
cues.zh: 如果我们改变

cues.en: that?
cues.zh: 这一点呢？

cues.zh: 那么这里我写了完全相同的代码，但不是用多态的

cues.en: way using c plus plus classes and virtual functions,
cues.zh: 方式，用 C++ 类和虚函数来写，

cues.en: I've written it using a standard enum and then just a shape type that effectively just unions them together. So even if something didn't have a height, for example, because it's only one parameter, well, has one now because we've done this the old fashioned way.
cues.zh: 我用了标准的 enum，然后只是一个 shape 类型，实际上就是把它们联合在一起。所以即使某个东西没有高度，比如因为它只有一个参数，好吧，现在它有一个了，因为我们用老式方法做了这件事。

cues.en: Then we say instead of getting the area from a virtual function, you're gonna get it from a switch statement. Exactly the thing that a clean code lecture would tell you never ever do. And what we would do here is we'd say switch on the type and depending on which of the types we have we will go ahead and compute the exact same thing that we were computing in the virtual function for the derived class of that type.
cues.zh: 然后我们说，不是从虚函数获取面积，而是从 switch 语句获取。正是整洁代码讲座会告诉你永远不要做的事。我们这里要做的是，对类型进行 switch，根据我们拥有的是哪种类型，我们就继续计算与该类型的派生类虚函数中完全相同的计算。

cues.en: Now we have effectively the exact same code. Here's the switch statement version of the exact same loop that we saw before for the Vtable version
cues.zh: 现在我们实际上有了完全相同的代码。这是与之前 Vtable 版本完全相同的循环的 switch 语句版本

cues.en: and what you can see is we loop over it and we just call the get area switch function instead of calling a function off of some pointer.
cues.zh: 你可以看到，我们遍历它，只是调用 get area switch 函数，而不是从某个指针调用函数。

cues.en: Now this offers us an immediate benefit which is that the shapes of course can just be in the array. There is no indirection of a pointer because they're all the same size. So we get that benefit. And then of course, we also get the benefit that the compiler can now see exactly what we're doing because it doesn't have to wonder about what kind of types might be derived from a base class. It can see everything that's in this code. So with those benefits,
cues.zh: 现在这为我们带来了一个即时的好处，那就是这些形状当然可以直接存放在数组中。由于它们的大小都一样，因此不存在指针的间接寻址。所以我们得到了这个好处。当然，我们还得到了另一个好处：编译器现在可以清楚地看到我们在做什么，因为它不必去猜想基类可能会派生出什么类型的子类。它能看清这段代码中的一切。所以有了这些好处，

cues.zh: 这条“整洁代码”的核心原则之一，我们得以将每个形状的耗时降至 24 个时钟周期，这意味着遵循第一条规则的“整洁代码”版本

cues.en: knowledge of what they were actually operating on to make themselves more efficient in aggregate. If you look back at the get area switch statement, one of the things that you can see is really these are all computing the exact same function just with a different coefficient. They're all going to do something like width times height or width times width, and then they're gonna multiply by half in the case of a triangle or pie in the case of a circle, something like this. Now one of the reasons that I think switch statements are great is because they actually show you this. It's really easy to pull out common patterns when you look at them put together by function rather than by class.
cues.zh: 它们实际操作的对象的信息，来让它们在总体上更加高效。如果你回看那个 get area 的 switch 语句，你会发现其中一件事是，它们其实都在计算完全相同的函数，只是系数不同。它们都会做类似“宽乘以高”或“宽乘以宽”的操作，然后在三角形的情况下乘以二分之一，或者在圆形的情况下乘以圆周率，诸如此类。现在，我认为 switch 语句很棒的原因之一，是因为它们确实把这些展现在了你面前。当你把它们按函数而不是按类归类放在一起看时，提取出共同的模式其实非常容易。
